<image1>
raw_record.answer: the southwest monsoon of the Indian Ocean
raw_record.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, one meridian labeled about 100°E and one latitude line labeled about 30°N can be seen. Within the region, there are many rivers that extend roughly north-south or nearly north-south; the January average temperature isolines are marked with values such as -12, -8, -4, and 0℃. The isotherms are obviously curved, showing that the terrain has large relief and has characteristics of a high-mountain and canyon area. Then reason: Combining the location near 100°E and near 30°N and the dense arrangement of rivers nearly north-south, this region can be judged to be the Hengduan Mountains area of southwest China or the southeastern margin of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. In this region, the water vapor for summer precipitation mainly comes from the direction of the Indian Ocean and is transported in by the southwest monsoon along canyon channels; therefore, the precipitation of this region mainly comes from the southwest monsoon of the Indian Ocean.
